title: Uniform vanishing for all conormal layers of an ample closed fibre
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] with a unique maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$, and put $k=A/\mathfrak m$. Let $g:X\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ be a proper morphism [def-weil-proper-morphism] of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $i:X_0=X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}A}\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ be the closed fibre [def-pc-fibre-product, def-pc-scheme-fibre], let $J=\mathfrak m\mathcal O_X$ be the extended ideal [def-nagata-extended-ideal], and let $N$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-sc-invertible-module]. Assume $i^*N$ is ample [def-pc-module-pullback, def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. Write $J^0=\mathcal O_X$ and use the ideal powers and quotient modules of [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module]. Then there is an integer $d_0\geq0$ such that, simultaneously for all integers $n\geq0$ and $d\geq d_0$, $$H^1\bigl(X,(J^n/J^{n+1})\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}N^{\otimes d}\bigr)=0.$$ Here tensor products and nonnegative tensor powers are those of [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product, def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module], and cohomology is that of [pqf-def-cohomology].

proof.text: The spectra of $A$ and $k$ are Noetherian: they have one affine chart with Noetherian coordinate ring and are quasi-compact. Here $k$ is Noetherian because the preimage of any ideal in $A/\mathfrak m$ is finitely generated in $A$ and the images of its generators generate the ideal. Properness includes finite type, so $X$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. The quotient map $A\to k$ induces a closed immersion $\operatorname{Spec}k\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-quotient-closed-immersion]; by [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf] its ideal sheaf is the quasi-coherent ideal $\widetilde{\mathfrak m}$ with global sections $\mathfrak m$. Hence, by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-ideal-closed-subscheme], the closed subscheme cut out by $\widetilde{\mathfrak m}$ is $\operatorname{Spec}k$ over $\operatorname{Spec}A$, and [lem-pc-closed-subscheme-base-change-ideal-image] identifies its base change $i$ as a closed immersion with ideal $J$. Being the ideal sheaf of a closed immersion, $J$ is a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf]. Its affine ideal is generated by the images of $\mathfrak m$ by [lem-pc-ideal-sheaf-comap-affine-extension]. Finally $g_0:X_0\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence], hence $X_0$ is Noetherian as well.

source.place: Tag 0D2M, lemma-ample-on-fibre, local-base and closed-fibre setup; Tags 01T6, 01JU, 01W4.

proof.text: Put $Q_n=J^n/J^{n+1}$. The ideal powers are quasi-coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-ideal-times-quasi-coherent-affine-sections]. The structure sheaf is coherent: it is quasi-coherent with the single generator $1$, so [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth] applies. Thus its quasi-coherent submodules $J^n$ and their quotients $Q_n$ are coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-kernel-cokernel-locnoeth]. Since $J J^n=J^{n+1}$, $JQ_n=0$. By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-coherent-equivalence](1), write $Q_n=i_*G_n$ with $G_n$ coherent on $X_0$. In particular $G_0=\mathcal O_{X_0}$. On an affine chart with coordinate ring $R$, $G_n$ is the module $(\mathfrak m R)^n/(\mathfrak m R)^{n+1}$ over $R/\mathfrak m R$.

source.place: Tag 0D2M, lemma-ample-on-fibre, paragraph beginning Let B; Tag 087T, lemma-i-star-equivalence; Tags 01XZ, 01Y1.

proof.text: Let $B=\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak m}(A)$. It is a commutative graded $k$-algebra, with multiplication induced by multiplication of representatives, by [lem-weil-pbc-associated-graded-ring-structure]. It is finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-associated-graded-finite-type], since $\mathfrak m$ is finitely generated. Put $\mathcal B=g_0^*\widetilde B$. Give $G=\bigoplus_{n\geq0}G_n$ its graded $\mathcal B$-action by $(a\bmod\mathfrak m^{r+1})(b\bmod J^{n+1})=g^\sharp(a)b\bmod J^{n+r+1}$. This is well-defined: changing either representative changes the product by $J^{n+r+1}$; addition, unit and associativity follow from those in the structure rings. These formulas commute with restriction, so they give, for each $r$ and $n$, an action of $B_r$ by $\mathcal O_X$-linear maps $Q_n\to Q_{n+r}$; by the full faithfulness in [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-coherent-equivalence](1) these are $\mathcal O_{X_0}$-linear maps $G_n\to G_{n+r}$. Since $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is one point, $g_0^{-1}\widetilde B$ is the constant sheaf $B$, so this $B$-action together with the $\mathcal O_{X_0}$-module structure is an action of $\mathcal B=\mathcal O_{X_0}\otimes_{g_0^{-1}\mathcal O}g_0^{-1}\widetilde B$. The sheaf $G$ is quasi-coherent: the finite partial sums $\bigoplus_{n\le M}G_n$ are quasi-coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-direct-sum], and $G$ is their directed colimit, so it is quasi-coherent with $G(U)=\bigoplus_nG_n(U)$ on affine opens $U$ by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-colimit-affine-sections]. It is generated by $1\in G_0$: on each affine chart $J^n(U)=(\mathfrak m R)^n=\mathfrak m^n R$, so every class is a finite sum of $R$-multiples of images of elements of $\mathfrak m^n$. The affine section formula in [lem-weil-pbc-ideal-times-quasi-coherent-affine-sections] justifies this calculation. Consequently $\mathcal B\to G$, $b\mapsto b\cdot1$, is a surjection, so $G$ is a finite type graded $\mathcal B$-module.

source.place: Tag 0D2M, lemma-ample-on-fibre, graded algebra and degree-zero generation; Tag 05GH, lemma-completion-Noetherian, finite degree-one generation.

proof.text: Write $L=i^*N$. It is invertible by [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor](1) and ample by hypothesis. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-formal-systems-graded-vanishing] to the Noetherian ring $k$, the proper morphism $g_0$, the finite type graded algebra $B$ and the graded module $G$ just constructed. There is one $d_0$, which we may increase to $\max(0,d_0)$, for which $H^1(X_0,G\otimes L^{\otimes d})=0$ for every $d\geq d_0$. For each $n$, the degree inclusion and projection $G_n\to G\to G_n$ compose to the identity. Tensoring and then applying $H^1$ preserves that identity. Thus $H^1(X_0,G_n\otimes L^{\otimes d})$ is a retract of zero and is zero, simultaneously for all $n$. This argument needs no interchange of cohomology with an infinite direct sum.

source.place: Tag 0D2M, lemma-ample-on-fibre, application of Tag 0897, lemma-graded-finiteness (2); degree retracts made explicit.

proof.text: For each $n,d$, apply [lem-pc-closed-immersion-coherent-cohomology] to $i$, $G_n$, and the invertible module $N^{\otimes d}$. Its projection formula identifies $Q_n\otimes N^{\otimes d}$ with $i_*(G_n\otimes i^*(N^{\otimes d}))$, and its cohomology comparison identifies $H^1$ of this pushforward with $H^1(X_0,G_n\otimes i^*(N^{\otimes d}))$. Iterating the tensor-pullback isomorphism in [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor](2), starting with the unit, gives $i^*(N^{\otimes d})\cong L^{\otimes d}$; (1) also gives invertibility of all the powers, including $d=0$. Therefore the last cohomology group is zero by step 4, with the very same $d_0$ for every $n$. This is the asserted vanishing on $X$.
